test_title: PYST 57: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 09 Sept, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following factors has least contributed to rural distress in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**High rural literacy levels**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **High rural literacy levels** have not significantly contributed to rural distress in India, as literacy is generally considered a positive factor aiding rural development.
 
• Literacy equips individuals with skills necessary for employment, entrepreneurship, and informed decision-making, reducing dependency on traditional agricultural practices.
 
• Rural literacy programs, such as Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, have been crucial in improving education and empowering rural communities to access government schemes and technological advancements.
 
• Increasing literacy rates in rural areas have encouraged diversification of income sources and a shift towards non-agricultural employment, reducing vulnerability to agricultural challenges.
 
• Thus, unlike other factors mentioned in the options, rural literacy levels contribute to alleviating distress rather than exacerbating it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fragmentation of land holdings**

 
 
• Land fragmentation refers to the division of agricultural land into smaller, uneconomical plots due to inheritance laws and population growth.
 
• Smaller land holdings make farming less viable, reduce economies of scale, and increase the cost of production.
 
• Fragmentation leads to reduced crop yields and limits the ability to adopt modern agricultural practices.
 
• This is a major contributor to rural distress as farmers struggle with inefficiency and lower income.
 
 
 
• **Declining productivity of rainfed agriculture**
 
 
• Rainfed agriculture depends on monsoon rains and constitutes approximately 60% of India’s cultivated land.
 
• Erratic rainfall patterns and climate change have led to declining productivity in rainfed areas, severely impacting farmers’ incomes.
 
• Rainfed regions often lack proper irrigation facilities, making them vulnerable to droughts and floods.
 
• This factor contributes significantly to rural distress, as a majority of small and marginal farmers rely on rainfed farming.
 
 
 
• **Post-harvest infrastructure shortages**
 
 
• India faces significant gaps in post-harvest infrastructure such as storage facilities, cold chains, and transportation networks.
 
• The lack of adequate infrastructure leads to high post-harvest losses, reducing farmers’ income and profitability.
 
• It also prevents farmers from accessing distant markets, forcing them to sell their produce at lower prices in local markets.
 
• Improving post-harvest infrastructure is crucial to reducing rural distress and enhancing farmers’ livelihoods.
